understanding.emotion: pulled in every direction and empty inside
understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call torn between duties, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: The mind that won't settle is not broken. It is pulled in every direction. The week gives it one chosen duty to hold, and the question of what you need to begin with.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the exhaustion of being needed by everyone and the emptiness of not knowing what you need.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that the mind cannot settle because duties are demanded, not chosen, and your own need has no voice.
week_beats.steady: You hold that your duty is to do what is right, not to please everyone, and that a clear mind is its own strength.
week_beats.act: You try choosing one duty for today, doing it fully, and asking yourself what you need before the next call.
week_beats.story: A son who had to choose between two duties shows you how choosing your own truth steadies the mind.

queries.hook: The weight of being needed by everyone and the exhaustion of not knowing what you need yourself, with the mind running in circles. My parents are getting older far away.
queries.diagnose: When duties pull in different directions and fear clouds which one is truly yours, the mind cannot settle; confusion grows from not choosing, only reacting.
queries.steady: Your duty is to do what is right, not to please everyone; the one who acts with a clear mind and steady heart is never truly alone.
queries.act: Choose one duty for today and do it fully, then let the rest go; ask yourself what you need before you answer the next call.
queries.story: A son and a brother who had to choose between two duties, and the one who chose his own truth found his footing.

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
verse.sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
verse.line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
verse.translation: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
verse.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

prasang.title: Mastering the mind
prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

verse.meaning: Arjuna tells Krishna that the mind is restless, turbulent, and stubborn, as hard to hold as the wind. Krishna agrees, saying that while the mind is difficult to master, it can be trained through practice and letting go. This is the confession of someone who has tried to force their mind into stillness and failed, and the beginning of a different approach.
verse.for_you: You are used to doing what is demanded. Today, look at the exhaustion beneath that doing. The mind will not settle because nothing has been chosen. Notice that emptiness. It is the first sign that a duty needs to be chosen, not just obeyed.

verse.speaker: Bhasa
verse.setting: Two childhood friends meet again in old age; one admits he never found peace.
verse.sanskrit: उह्यमानमनन्तेषु चेतः कार्यमहोर्मिषु । क्षणमेति न विश्रान्तिं चिन्ताताण्डविताशयम् ॥ इदं कृतं करोमीदं करिष्यामीदमित्यलम् । कलनाजालवलिता मूर्च्छिता मतिपक्षिणी ॥
verse.line: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.
verse.translation: Carried along on endless great waves of tasks, the mind never gets a moment's rest; its depths dance with worry. 'This I've done, this I'm doing, this I'll do': so the bird of the mind, tangled in a net of reckonings, faints.
verse.why: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

prasang.title: Two old friends meet again and admit they never found peace
prasang.summary: Bhasa and Vilasa grow up inseparable in a forest hermitage. After their fathers die they drift apart and spend long lonely years in hard austerities. When they meet again as old men, one asks if the other is well; he answers honestly that there is no wellness while the mind keeps spinning through endless tasks and worries.
prasang.story_hook: They had been inseparable as boys, and when they met again they were old men with nothing to show.
prasang.lesson: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

verse.meaning: Two old friends meet again after many years. One admits he has never found peace. He says he has spent his life caught in endless tasks. He thinks about what he has done, what he is doing, and what he must do next. The mind is carried along on great waves of work. It dances with worry. It is like a bird tangled in a net, fainting from the reckoning. Years of hard effort without understanding leave a person exactly where they started.
verse.for_you: You are living inside that endless list. The work is not the only thing pulling you. It is the voice that never stops, and the part of you that has no voice at all. That is why nothing settles.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on inner stillness in an active life.
verse.sanskrit: बहिःकृत्रिमसंरंभो हृदि संरम्भवर्जितः । कर्ता बहिरकर्तान्तर्लोके विहर शुद्धधीः ॥
verse.line: Be busy on the outside and unhurried inside. Act fully, but don't let it agitate you.
verse.translation: Outwardly busy, inwardly free of agitation; a doer on the outside, a non-doer within: move through the world with a clear mind.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.meaning: Ribhu is speaking to Nidagha. He has just finished explaining that the world is not as solid as it seems, and now he is telling Nidagha how to live in it. He says to be busy on the outside and unhurried inside. Act fully, but do not let it agitate you. The wise person does what is in front of them, speaks gently, and moves through the world with a clear mind, treating everyone as kin.
verse.for_you: The calls to Dubai and the calls home both demand your full attention. You can be busy on the outside, moving through each conversation, but unhurried inside. Let the next call wait while you finish the one before it. Do not let the noise of others' needs agitate you.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how the wise live and work.
verse.sanskrit: निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः । शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
verse.line: Expecting nothing, mind steady, letting go of possessiveness, you can work without being stained.
verse.translation: Without hope, with mind and self controlled, giving up all possessiveness, doing only bodily action, he incurs no fault.
verse.why: Contentment and freedom from envy let you work without being bound.

prasang.title: How the great yogis live
prasang.summary: The wise act without selfish motive, content and dependent on nothing, free from envy, steady in success and failure.
prasang.lesson: Contentment and freedom from envy let you work without being bound.

verse.for_you: You carry the weight of your father's surgery and your brother's wedding, but your mind can stay steady. Do your part for your family without letting the pressure of their expectations stain your own rest.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna, who asks why he must act at all if understanding is higher.
verse.sanskrit: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः । शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः ॥
verse.line: Do the work that's yours. Doing something beats doing nothing; even living needs action.
verse.translation: Do your allotted work, for action is better than inaction. Even the maintenance of your body would not be possible without action.
verse.why: Not acting is still a choice; do the work that is yours.

prasang.title: Why doing your duty without attachment is better
prasang.summary: Arjuna is confused and asks for one clear answer. Krishna says no one can stop acting, that repressing the body while the mind indulges is self-deception, and that action beats inaction.
prasang.lesson: Not acting is still a choice; do the work that is yours.

verse.for_you: Ask what is right, not what is easy; choose your own duty with a clear mind and carry it out without fear.

verse.speaker: Medhavin
verse.setting: A young man named Medhavin urges his father not to keep postponing what truly matters.
verse.sanskrit: श्वः कार्यमद्य कुर्वीत पूर्वाह्णे चापराह्णिकम् / नहि प्रतीक्षते मृत्युः कृतमस्य न वा कृतम्
verse.line: Do tomorrow's work today, and the afternoon's in the morning. Time doesn't wait for you to be ready.
verse.translation: Do tomorrow's work today, and the afternoon's work in the morning. Death does not wait to see whether your work is done or not.
verse.why: Life slips away while we stay busy. Do what matters now.
verse.misuse: About not postponing what matters, not about working nonstop.

prasang.title: Medhavin: the son who woke his father
prasang.summary: A father lays out the conventional path of study, family and ritual. His son Medhavin replies that days and nights fall like arrows and death takes people mid-task, so do tomorrow's work today and live truthfully now.
prasang.lesson: Life slips away while we stay busy. Do what matters now.

verse.meaning: A young man named Medhavin tells his father that time does not pause for readiness. The father speaks of a life of study and ritual, but Medhavin replies that days pass like arrows and death comes before our work is done. He says to do tomorrow's work today, and the afternoon's work in the morning. Life slips away while we wait to be prepared, so do what matters now.
verse.for_you: This morning, choose one call and give it your full attention. After it ends, sit with one quiet question: what do I need before the next one comes? That single choice is your work today.

story.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
story.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
story.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
story.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

anchor.speaker: Janaka
anchor.setting: King Janaka, alone on his palace roof after overhearing wandering sages, rethinks his life.
anchor.sanskrit: संपदश्च विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेच्चित्तेन संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा हन्त मन्ये महापदः ॥ आपदोऽपि विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेन्मनसि संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा मन्ये मनसि संपदः ॥
anchor.line: Good fortune the mind clutches becomes trouble. Trouble the mind accepts becomes a kind of fortune.
anchor.translation: All those dazzling fortunes, if the mind clings to them, are really great calamities in grand disguise. And all those varied misfortunes, if the mind accepts them, are really fortunes.
anchor.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
anchor.misuse: Accepting a hardship doesn't mean not fixing what can be fixed.

script: You are pulled in every direction and you are empty inside. You spend hours on the phone and the work never stops. Nothing is your own right now.
Arjuna, the warrior, tells Krishna, the charioteer, that his mind is restless and stubborn. Krishna agrees. Arjuna said:
चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम्, तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम्.
In plain words: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.

Arjuna tells Krishna that the mind is restless, turbulent, and stubborn, as hard to hold as the wind. Krishna agrees, saying that while the mind is difficult to master, it can be trained through practice and letting go. This is the confession of someone who has tried to force their mind into stillness and failed, and the beginning of a different approach.
When you hang up the phone today, do not reach for the next thing. Sit with that emptiness for a few minutes. Let the mind rest without deciding what to do next.
Can you let the mind rest without asking it to solve anything?

depth.life: You are in Dubai, sending money for eleven years. Your father had heart surgery this year, your brother got married, and your wife wants to go back to India. You are on the phone four hours a day. Your parents are getting older far away. You feel pulled in every direction and empty inside.
depth.points: The mind is restless and stubborn. It cannot be forced into stillness. It must be trained by practice and letting go. The emptiness you feel is not a lack of love. It is the absence of a chosen direction. You have been obeying demands, not choosing a duty for yourself.
depth.practice: Sit quietly for five minutes today. Do not try to stop your thoughts. Just notice where your mind goes without following it.
depth.question: What is one small duty you could choose for yourself today?
